correspondence.finding: The western start corresponds to small mapped waters close to the northern sheet border. The route runs east and southeast through the pond-and-stream chain adjoining the southern side of the Falloon Lake complex. The source shows these minor water connections; no individual head-stream name is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Central Manitoba elongated-lake and southern bend
correspondence.finding: The selected chain continues through narrow, irregular lakes north of Savage Lake, bends southeast, then turns north along connected waters on the western side of the Nabel Lake complex. The intervening lake arms and stream links are visible. Nearby named lakes are distinguished rather than inherited as river names.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.finding: Mapped connected waters continue east from the Nabel-area complex toward the boundary. The southeastern corner of Edehon Lake sheet 65A supplies the short continuation north of the Manitoba boundary, including the small lake-and-stream connection leading east into the adjoining Hyde Lake sheet.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.finding: Hyde Lake sheet 55D shows the entering stream chain continuing east through low lakes, turning north and then northeast along a sequence of lakes and channels into the southern arm/outlet setting of labeled Geillini Lake. The route is not inferred merely from the nearby lake label; the intervening mapped waters were inspected.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Geillini Lake outlet and middle river
correspondence.finding: The southern Geillini Lake passage connects to the eastward river. The mapped river bends southeast through further small lakes and channels; the cartographic label Geillini extends along this downstream corridor. Geillini Lake and Geillini River remain different geographic components.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Lower river and actual sea terminal
correspondence.finding: The river continues east across the low coastal plain to the mapped Hudson Bay shore. The lower reach, coastal marsh/pond setting, outlet channel and sea are visible on the original sheet. The inherited sea-terminal classification is consistent with the mapped setting at ordinary corridor scale; no exact mouth-point or shoreline agreement is claimed.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.finding: The selected Sierra de las Minas headward course approaches Chilascó from the east through the Concepción valley near San José/El Ceibillal. It turns north as Chilascó, meets Sinanjá near San José El Espinero, then follows Sinanjá northeast to the Panimá corridor. Eastward below the Ribacó junction near Argelia, the route is Matanzas, joining Polochic south of La Tinta and continuing toward Telemán/Panzós. The Polochic approach from Tucurú is not the selected headwater.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: A multi-name component; the initial small source extension has no separately established name. Río La Concepción in the Ribacó prose is a different branch. No precise name-transition vertex is asserted.

correspondence.finding: Short Polochic continuation in the Panzós lowland, ending in the broad Cahabón confluence setting. Its split from10584 is rendered metadata, not a source-named river boundary.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.finding: Below the Cahabón junction the route follows lower Polochic east through the Panzós–El Estor lowland into the western end of Lago de Izabal. The selected straight lake passage crosses toward the northeast outlet. Río Dulce continues through its upper constriction, the broad El Golfete waterbody, and the lower winding gorge to the Caribbean coast at Livingston. The actual terminal is beyond both lake passages, not at the Polochic lake mouth.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: Composite river–lake–river component. Lake-crossing model lines are connectors within waterbodies, not uniformly named river reaches.

correspondence.finding: The western selected start is a through-reach in the Cobán setting, continuing east through San Pedro Carchá. It turns northeast toward the Lanquín/Semuc Champey corridor and then east south of Santa María Cahabón. It does not represent Cahabón’s complete natural-source route; upstream Tactic/Santa Cruz reaches lie outside the selection.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: Selected Cahabón through-corridor; the river name is not reassigned to the other mainstem feeder.

correspondence.finding: Continues the same Cahabón eastward through the Oxec confluence sector and then southeast via the Seguamó/Cahaboncito approach to Polochic. Independent project sources establish the Oxec II dam and reservoir on this Cahabón corridor. Río Oxec is a distinct incoming branch; the selection does not continue up it.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope: Cahabón identity persists through the impounded corridor; no exact modern reservoir footprint or dam-position fit is claimed.

correspondence.finding: The selected head lies northeast of Malbrán near the Route 43 setting, south of the separately mapped meandering valley near Los Chañares and El Dos del Salado. It runs generally southeast between the Malbrán railway/Route 34 corridor and the El Palmar country. The original 1:250,000 map shows fields, wooded/grassland patches and local wet ground, with no named source river or continuous channel following the selection. The intervening land is visible, so no missing connector is being supplied by a nearby river label.
correspondence.correspondence: Full source/headward setting and initial southeast course read at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Argentina station, transport crossing and Laguna El Mojón Colorado
correspondence.finding: East of Argentina station the selected path turns south through the broad mapped marsh plain, then crosses the Route 34 and railway corridor north of Palo Negro and turns southwest into the elongated setting labeled Laguna El Mojón Colorado. The lake is shown with shallow/wetland hatching rather than as a single named river channel. The course then leaves its southwestern part into the surrounding wet plain.
correspondence.correspondence: Full bend, transport crossing, named lagoon setting and southwest continuation visible in the original north panel and overview.

correspondence.component_scope: El Huaico, western side of Laguna Beltrán and Los Porongos country
correspondence.finding: The line continues southwest through wet ground southeast of El Huaico, turns south west of the separately labeled Laguna Beltrán, and passes the Route 15 setting. It then bends through the El Mojón/Villa Los Porongos country, staying east of the separately mapped Laguna de los Porongos. Near Los Jagüeles it crosses a small unnamed lake/wet-depression setting east of the settlement before continuing south through marshy intervening ground. Neither Beltrán nor Porongos is a hydronym for the selected full course.
correspondence.correspondence: Overlapping north and middle panels show the complete southwest/south turn, nearby distinct lakes and the actual selected wetland passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Las Ramaditas and northern lake/wetland transition
correspondence.finding: South of Los Jagüeles the selected path passes east of Campo Las Ramaditas and turns east/southeast through the low country west of the Borde de los Altos and Mackinlay. The 1:250,000 mosaic depicts this lower passage within a broad northern extension of Laguna Mar Chiquita. The 1:500,000 overview instead depicts several separate lobed lakes surrounded by wetland along this same corridor. Both sources show the full selected geography; their different inundation representations are retained without imposing precise contemporaneous shorelines or inferring an undocumented hydraulic connection.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete mapped wetland, intervening low ground and lake passage at two original scales.

correspondence.finding: The selected route reaches the eastern side of the wetland/lake complex west of Mackinlay and Mackinlay Sur, then turns south past the Los Pioneros and Campo Busso/Yarará settings, alongside the landform labeled Borde de los Altos or Altos de Mar Chiquita. The 1:250,000 map places the passage within continuous lake water, whereas the overview shows marsh and an isolated lake near Los Pioneros before the selected line enters the main open-water lake near Yarará. No separately named river mouth or reservoir passage is established.
correspondence.correspondence: The full approach and transition to the main receiving lake are visible on the overlapping middle/terminal panels and full overview.

correspondence.component_scope: Long lake-interior passage and actual terminal northwest of La Paquita
correspondence.finding: After the Yarará setting the selected line continues south inside eastern Laguna Mar Chiquita, roughly parallel to its eastern shore west of Morteros and Campo Grosso/El Rancho. It finally bends southwest and ends inside the southeastern lake basin northwest of La Paquita, west of the Colonia Doso/Dosolina country. The final endpoint is in the named lake, not on a mapped outlet, a river confluence or the nearby southern Arroyo del Saladillo. The lake name is established for this terminal component only.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire long lake passage and the actual ending read directly in both original map scales.

correspondence.finding: Bucher, Gavier Pizarro and Curto distinguish the southern Mar Chiquita lake from the northern Bañados del Río Dulce complex of wetlands, grasslands and salares. Their original 2004 Figure 4 and pp.17–19 describe an eastern chain of lagoons/wetlands bending northeast toward the Bajo del borde oriental and an ancient Salado connection, separate from the central Dulce and western Saladillos corridors. Pages21–22 describe the raised eastern margin and the very low, variable northern shore with muddy/saline flats. These are regional explanations for the mapped plain–wetland–lake mixture, not evidence that every selected part has one river name or a present surface connection to Salado.
correspondence.correspondence: Original Figure4 inspected; prose read on printed pp.15–22. Figure captions or search snippets are not substituted for the detailed IGN observations.

finding: The starting fragment occupies a mapped northern tributary–Gordito junction setting and turns toward the eastern head/boundary segment. The tributary is not independently named.
The natural Gordito channel is mapped separately downstream toward Las Cuevas. This fragment does not establish a name for the following eastern excursion.
correspondence.correspondence: Whole short initial fragment considered against original MMA hydrography and the field-study Gordito head setting.
correspondence.geographic_correspondence: Bounded tributary/junction setting accounted for; no whole-fragment scalar hydronym established.

finding: Its broad eastern bulge follows the mapped international-boundary/upland setting rather than the interior Gordito valley. The natural river instead runs toward the separately mapped Gordito–Las Cuevas junction.

The retained border-aligned flag is only model metadata. The scope decision rests on the independently visible border shape, terrain and channel separation, without asserting exact boundary or vertex agreement.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire southeast-then-southwest eastern excursion lies in the inspected headward hydrographic and field-study relief/border views.
correspondence.geographic_correspondence: Completed mapped noncontinuous-river/boundary-corridor observation, not an unread connector.

finding: The initial northwest return cuts across the Gordito valley and adjoining upland setting to reach Grande above its westward course. It is not the natural Gordito continuation to the Las Cuevas confluence.

The field-study map identifies Grande below the natural Gordito–Las Cuevas junction. The downstream selected route passes the Colorado and Palillos settings, then the Tascadero, Mostazal and Rapel junctions.

Grande continues past Ponio into the northern/eastern La Paloma approach. The reservoir receives the Guatulame arm from the south; the selected route exits northwest and follows lower Grande to Hurtado.

At Grande–Hurtado near Ovalle the receiving course becomes Limarí. The lower corridor passes the Ingenio/La Placa and Punitaqui settings and reaches its coastal estuary. The MMA coastal waterbody/land margin supports the actual Pacific terminal at generalized scale.
correspondence.correspondence: Full return connector and subsequent Grande–La Paloma–Grande–Limarí course to the coast inspected.
correspondence.name_scope: Multiple component identities; no single scalar name assigned to the entire FID.
correspondence.geographic_correspondence: Complete bounded coverage; includes the initial noncontinuous-river connector and the supported natural downstream river/reservoir course.
